\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write the personal-information task inside the published DELE A1 timing and word count, and mark it against the published criteria.}

Complete ES-W01-con-reloj: write the four lines in three minutes, count the words against the published 15-25 range, and mark task fulfilment before style.

\section[Practice]{The same four lines, with a clock}

\label{lesson:ES-W01-con-reloj}



\begin{quote}
You wrote four lines about yourself with as long as you liked.

A task you can only do untimed is not yet a task you can do. Here are the exam's own conditions.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — timed composition}
\textbf{What the exam publishes.} The DELE A1 writing paper runs \textbf{25 minutes} and holds \textbf{two} tasks. The first is a personal-information form asking for \textbf{15 to 25 words}. No dictionary. No phone. You write in the booklet you are given.

That is one task out of two, so give it its share and no more: \textbf{three minutes}, starting now.

Write the four lines about yourself, then close with the courtesy word.

When the three minutes are up, stop writing even if a line is unfinished. An unfinished paper is information; an untimed one is not.

\textbf{Now mark your own.} The published criteria for this task are two, and they are worth knowing in this order:

1. \textbf{Did you do what was asked?} Four facts and a close, nothing else. 2. \textbf{Can it be read?} Language a stranger at a desk would understand. Not elegant language — understandable language.

Count your words. Under fifteen and the task is half done; well past twenty-five and you spent time you did not have. Both are worth knowing before an examiner tells you.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} your four lines aloud, at the pace you wrote them
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which of the two published criteria comes first — doing what was asked, or writing beautifully? (\textbf{Doing what was asked.})

You have now written to a clock, to a word count, and to a stated standard, with no Spanish you did not already own.
\end{tcolorbox}
